mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% per month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by 2% or more.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate above 8% for three consecutive months signals persistent labor market slack, which depresses wage growth and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by at least 1% per month for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by at least 1% for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12mo MA and CPIAUCSL > 12mo MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both real personal income (proxied by RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) of at least 1% each for two consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in household demand, which reduces consumption and investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both fall by at least 1% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both RSAFS and HOUST decline by at least 1% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 0.5% month-over-month for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > +0.5% month-over-month for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS grows by more than 0.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized GDP growth rate (GDPC1) below 1% for three consecutive quarters indicates subpar economic growth, which reduces corporate profit expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of strong monetary easing.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 1% annualized for three consecutive quarters
regime_hint: subpar growth, except during monetary easing
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 is below 1% for three consecutive quarters and monetary easing is not present.
